=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 776-789 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The idempotency check treats any issue comment containing the session’s cap marker as proof that the hook posted its blocker, without verifying the comment’s author or that it contains the blocker marker.
  WHY: A comment containing the session marker can suppress the actionable blocker comment while the hook adds the label and records the blocker as posted; z-ai_glm-5_2 disagrees that this is a defect because it considers the session ID an adequate safeguard.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: line 903, `outcome = retried or publish_cap_blocker(...)` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: When a pending retry returns a truthy result, the `or` expression skips the cap path’s own `publish_cap_blocker` call, including when the retry failed.
  WHY: The source issue may receive no fresh blocker publish attempt when the cap is reached during a failing retry; z-ai_glm-5_2 considers this intentional to avoid doubling API calls beyond the hook timeout, while the flagged reviewers say it contradicts the planned cap behavior.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 873-874; lines 866-874 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A `GuardStateError` during the pending-retry block returns from `evaluate` before the transcript check and cap-blocker publication path run.
  WHY: With corrupted state, a stop at the cap can be allowed with a warning without reaching those checks; deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro notes that the early fail-open is consistent with the documented contract, while qwen_qwen3_7-plus flags the skipped checks and publication.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 884-887; lines 883-887 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: A pending-retry summary can still be emitted when the current turn has no question or has already posted a verified blocker.
  WHY: The system message can describe a retry from a prior stop alongside a no-question or already-blocked return; deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro says this is informative and causes no functional harm.
- CLAUDE.md: CLAUDE.md §28.G cap-blocker bullet (~line 2383-2396); agents.md: agents.md "Log lines" line (~1195) | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The documentation omits the 6-second per-call timeout from CLAUDE.md and is reported to omit the `cap_blocker_already_posted` event from the documented log-event set.
  WHY: The findings say the omissions make the log event set and per-call budget harder to verify; z-ai_glm-5_2 disputes the event omission, stating the `already_posted` path returns before `_append_cap_log`, but confirms the timeout is absent from CLAUDE.md.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Phase 1 — cap blocker publish in the unattended question guard … `publish_cap_blocker`, injectable `runner` / `sleep`, pending retry at the top of the `Stop` path" (docs/plans/issue-5083-guard-cap-source-issue-blocker-plan.md:121-164; docs/implement-plan/issue-5083-guard-cap-source-issue-blocker.md:16-25)
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py, `evaluate` cap-path publish invocation
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The cap path at line 903 computes `outcome = retried or publish_cap_blocker(...)`; the test `test_pending_retry_is_not_repeated_by_the_cap_path_in_the_same_stop` (tests/test_unattended_question_guard.py:988-997) asserts that no fresh cap-path publish is attempted when the pending retry runs and fails.
- requirement: "Every outcome appends one `cap_blocker_*` line to the cap log" (PR description; mirrored in workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py module docstring at the "Cap blocker" block).
  expected_change_site: CLAUDE.md §28.G cap-blocker bullet; agents.md "Log lines"
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `publish_cap_blocker` can return `{"status": "already_posted", "attempts": 0, "error": None}`; the cap-log event it emits is `cap_blocker_already_posted`; the PR CHANGED FILES list and the diff for CLAUDE.md / agents.md list only `cap_blocker_posted`, `cap_blocker_exists`, `cap_blocker_failed`, `cap_blocker_invalid`.
- requirement: "Each call bounded by CAP_BLOCKER_CALL_TIMEOUT" (workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py module docstring, "Cap blocker (issue #5083)" block, line ~65) — the bound is `CAP_BLOCKER_CALL_TIMEOUT = 6.0`.
  expected_change_site: CLAUDE.md §28.G cap-blocker bullet (added lines ~2383-2396)
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The CLAUDE.md bullet describes "up to 3 times within the hook (1 s and 2 s backoff, a 24 s budget inside the 30 s wiring timeout)" but does not state the per-call timeout; agents.md does ("6 s per call, 24 s budget").

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: line 781, `if cap_marker in out:` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The idempotency check accepts any issue comment containing the session’s cap marker without verifying its author or that its body starts with `BLOCKED_COMMENT_MARKER`.
  WHY: A comment containing the marker can suppress the fixed-template blocker comment while the hook adds the label and records the blocker as posted.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: line 903, `outcome = retried or publish_cap_blocker(...)` | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A truthy pending-retry result short-circuits the cap path’s `publish_cap_blocker` call, including when that retry failed.
  WHY: When a session reaches the cap while a pending retry fails, the cap path makes no fresh publish attempt and the source issue may receive no blocker.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 873-874, `except GuardStateError as exc: return _warn(str(exc))` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A `GuardStateError` during pending-retry state reads returns before the transcript check and cap-blocker publication path.
  WHY: A stop at the cap with corrupted state skips those checks and publication; the source also notes this is consistent with the documented fail-open contract.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py: lines 884-887, `if kind is None: return retry_message` and `if blocked_comment_posted(...): return retry_message` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A pending-retry summary is returned even when the current turn has no question or has already posted a verified blocker.
  WHY: The message describes an action for a prior stop, though the source says it remains informative and causes no functional harm.
- CLAUDE.md, agents.md: CLAUDE.md §28.G cap blocker bullet (~line 2383-2396); agents.md "Log lines" line (~1195) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The docs are reported to omit the `cap_blocker_already_posted` event and CLAUDE.md omits the per-call timeout documented in agents.md.
  WHY: Operators may not recognize the reported event, and the per-call budget cannot be independently verified from CLAUDE.md.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Phase 1 — cap blocker publish in the unattended question guard … `publish_cap_blocker`, injectable `runner` / `sleep`, pending retry at the top of the `Stop` path" (docs/plans/issue-5083-guard-cap-source-issue-blocker-plan.md:121-164; docs/implement-plan/issue-5083-guard-cap-source-issue-blocker.md:16-25)
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/unattended_question_guard.py, `evaluate` cap-path publish invocation at line 903
  Evidence of absence: The cap path at line 903 computes `outcome = retried or publish_cap_blocker(...)`. When `retried` is a truthy dict (which it always is — `publish_cap_blocker` always returns a dict), `publish_cap_blocker` is never called. The plan requires the cap path to publish the blocker when the cap is reached. The `or` short-circuit means the cap path can report a stale retry failure from the top-of-evaluate pending-retry attempt without making its own attempt. The test `test_pending_retry_is_not_repeated_by_the_cap_path_in_the_same_stop` locks this behavior: it asserts that when a pending retry runs with all GETs failing and the cap path is reached, only the retry's GET calls happen, not the cap path's own `publish_cap_blocker` post_comment + label calls. The test name says "not repeated" confirming the intent that the cap path intentionally skips its own publish. This contradicts the plan requirement that `publish_cap_blocker` be called at the cap to ensure a blocker reaches the source issue.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
